<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par113 />equally well be represented by a ''substantive'' of kindred stem.<ref>On these substantives (and on the use of the infinitive absolute generally as absolute object, see above, m), cf. the ''schema etymologicum'' treated in connexion with the government of the verb in {{GHGpar|117|p}}, q.</ref> In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=14}} the substantive intensifying the verb is found ''along with'' the infinitive absolute.

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|x}}
5. Instead of the infinitive absolute immediately connected with the finite verb, an infinitive construct form appears (cf. {{GHGpar|73|d}}), in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=25}} ({{GHGheb|text=גַּם קֹב}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=גַּם שֹׁל}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=34}} ({{GHGheb|text=רִיב יָרִיב}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=בִּין תָּבִין}}). In the last instances the infinitive is probably assimilated to the imperfect, like the infinitive Niphʿal in the forms noticed in {{GHGpar|51|k}} and note.—Cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=3|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּבֹ֫אוּ בֹא וְהַכּוֹת}} (read so with the LXX) before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, hence, no doubt due to the dislike of a hiatus; so in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=50|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=1|verse=7}} ({{GHGheb|text=הֲבֹל}}), all in rapid style; ''after'' the verb, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=7}}, unless {{GHGheb|text=הַֽעֲבֵיר}} is intended.

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|y}}
'''4.''' Finally the infinitive absolute sometimes appears as ''a substitute for the finite verb'', either when it is sufficient simply to mention the verbal idea (see z), or when the hurried or otherwise excited style intentionally contents itself with this infinitive, in order to bring out the verbal idea in a clearer and more expressive manner (see aa).

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|z}}
(''a'') The infinitive absolute as the continuation of a preceding finite verb. In the later books especially it often happens that in a succession of several acts only the first (or sometimes more) of the verbs is inflected, while the second (or third, &c.) is added simply in the infinitive absolute. Thus after several perfects, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=5}} (cf. verse 11) ''we have sinned ... and have transgressed thy law'', {{GHGheb|text=וִסוֹר|translate=and have turned aside}} (prop. ''a turning aside'' took place); so after a {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=36|verse=7}} (?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=14|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=19|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=1|verse=6}} (four infinitives), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=3|verse=4}} (but read with Wellhausen, after the LXX, {{GHGheb|text=וְהַלְבִּ֫שׁוּ אֹתוֹ}}), 7:5, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=8|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=9|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=3|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, 16, 18, 12:6 ff., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=8}}, 13, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=5|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=19}};<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=7|verse=14}} a perfect appears to be continued by means of an infinitive construct; but the text is quite corrupt; Cornill reads {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְעוּ תָקוֹעַ הָכִ֫ינוּ הָכֵן}}.</ref> after the {{GHGterm|perfect consecutive}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=12|verse=10}}; after the {{GHGterm|perfect frequentative}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=9|verse=25}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=וְהִקְטִיר}} be intended); after the simple {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=25|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=30|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=44}} (three infinitives), 36:23, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=21|verse=24}}; after a ''cohortative'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=20}}; after the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=43}} (as a continuation of {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּרְכֵּב}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=7|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=37|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=8|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=16|verse=36}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=7|verse=3}}; with {{GHGheb|text=אוֹ|translate=or}} after the {{GHGterm|jussive}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=14|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=2|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=6|verse=9|hidebook=1}}; after the {{GHGterm|imperative}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=30}}b, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=4|verse=4}}f.; after the {{GHGterm|participle}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=15}} (strengthened by {{GHGheb|text=אַף}}, and regarded, like the participle itself, as an adverbial accusative); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=8|verse=8}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|aa}}
